assets/vo/s01-a1e7ac1c.mp3: This pilot approves code from his phone.
assets/vo/s01-9deaa87a.mp3: His dev team? All AI agents.
assets/vo/s01-895cb6e1.mp3: Five things to know. The last one matters most.
assets/vo/s02-adb7256e.mp3: One: AI went from autocomplete to whole features.
assets/vo/s02-0574b7ab.mp3: It reads your code, writes it, tests it, and merges.
assets/vo/s03-5cbfd206.mp3: Two: don't just prompt. Write a spec:
assets/vo/s03-20e8bdaf.mp3: what to build, and what done looks like.
assets/vo/s04-be9dc713.mp3: Three: go from coder to conductor.
assets/vo/s04-a8dcb3fd.mp3: You make the big calls, and split the work for agents.
assets/vo/s05-ddb38035.mp3: Your code, tools, skills and MCP servers share one limited window.
assets/vo/s06-a84ad570.mp3: And loops: set the goal, then let the agent loop until it's done.
assets/vo/s07-54f05be6.mp3: Five, the big one: prompt injection.
assets/vo/s07-592394d4.mp3: Hidden text in a pull request can trick an agent into leaking your keys.
assets/vo/s07-d02c48c0.mp3: So run agents in a sandbox.
assets/vo/s08-7f29915b.mp3: Developers aren't going away. They're becoming conductors.
